question: Name the exact mechanism by which the production native tracker projects a MOVING mob's position, and whether that projection diverges from the wire.

mechanism.name: TIME-SLICE MIXING IN THE MELEE GATE: the tracked mob cell is the mob's PRE-WALK cell (frozen for the whole walk), the tracked self cell is the agent's POST-WALK cell (jumped to the walk destination), and the gate compares those two different moments. The server rejects every such swing with 0x0139 ZC_ATTACK_FAILURE_FOR_DISTANCE, and no production code path ingests 0x0139, so the miss is silent.
mechanism.one_line: native_gameplay._actor stores a moving mob at its PRE-WALK cell (the 0x09FD from-cell) while native_gameplay._self_position stores the agent at its POST-WALK cell (the 0x0087 destination); scripts._melee_action then reads 'adjacent' on that mixture, and the server answers 0x0139 which production never ingests.

why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.server_move_frame: clif.cpp:2064-2090 clif_move() -> clif_set_unit_walking(*bl, nullptr, ud, AREA_WOS) -> 0x09FD ZC_NOTIFY_MOVEENTRY to every client in the area
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.server_move_payload: clif.cpp:1369+ WBUFPOS2(&p.MoveData[0], 0, bl.x, bl.y, ud.to_x, ud.to_y, ud.sx, ud.sy): MoveData[0..2] = the unit's CURRENT cell, MoveData[2..4] = the walk's FINAL TARGET
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.server_emission_rate: unit.cpp:238-246 unit_walktoxy_nextcell(): clif_move()/clif_walkok() are called ONLY under `if (sendMove || DIFF_TICK(tick, ud->dmg_tick) < MOVE_REFRESH_TIME)`, i.e. ONCE per walk, not once per cell step. unit.cpp:186-192 sends the final zero-length walkok when the path ends.
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.packing_helpers: clif.cpp:177-185 WBUFPOS2 / clif.cpp:213-239 RBUFPOS2 (the 6-byte MoveData layout)
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.self_walk_payload: clif.cpp:2052-2060 clif_walkok() -> WBUFPOS2(packet.moveData, 0, sd.x, sd.y, sd.ud.to_x, sd.ud.to_y, 8, 8): the 0x0087 destination is the walk's FINAL TARGET too
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.server_range_check: unit.cpp:3254-3264: range = sstatus->rhw.range (1 for the pinned Novice); `if (sd && !check_distance_client_bl(src,target,range)) { clif_movetoattack(*sd,*target); return 1; }`
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.server_metric: path.hpp:48 + path.cpp:485-521: check_distance_client = distance_client = (int)(Euclidean(dx,dy) - 0.1) <= range -> the client-style CIRCULAR metric, NOT Chebyshev. Range 1 accepts only the 8 adjacent cells (Euclidean 1.0/1.414).
why_the_wire_lets_this_happen.server_verdict_frame: clif.cpp:8172-8186 clif_movetoattack() -> 0x0139 ZC_ATTACK_FAILURE_FOR_DISTANCE carrying targetAID, the server's target x/y, the server's self x/y and the attack range

production_code_path.mob_projection: src/robots/adapters/native_gameplay.py:595-608 _actor(): offset = 63 if p.packet_id == 0x09FD else 59; _position(raw, 63, ...) decodes the MoveData FROM-cell. The destination (bytes 65..67 of the same frame) is never decoded anywhere in src/.
production_code_path.self_projection: src/robots/adapters/native_gameplay.py:720-746 _self_position(): for 0x0087 it decodes the DESTINATION (`destination = (((b & 15) << 6) | (c >> 2), ((c & 3) << 8) | d)`) and sets _position to it, with the comment 'the tracked position must be the walk DESTINATION, not the from-cell'.
production_code_path.state_projection: src/robots/app/playing_runtime.py:1904-1937 _nearby(): ActorRef.x/y = the tracker's actor cell; ActorRef.distance = math.hypot(actor.position - tracked self position).
production_code_path.the_gate: src/robots/app/scripts.py:477-493 _melee_action(): `if max(abs(x - state.x), abs(y - state.y)) <= MELEE_RANGE: return Attack(target_id=target.id)` - MELEE_RANGE=1, CHEBYSHEV, over the two stale projections.
production_code_path.silent_feedback: no handler for 0x0139 exists anywhere under src/robots/ (grep: only a docstring mention in scripts.py:59 and scripts.py:484). The frame arrives on the wire and is dropped by the tracker, so an out-of-range swing is indistinguishable from a miss.
production_code_path.documented_metric: src/robots/app/scripts.py:53-60 already records that the server range-checks with the circular client metric and that '1 on the server's own metric is the only known-accepted boundary' - the gate is right, but it is fed stale cells.

answers_to_the_briefs_hypotheses.mob_positions_may_not_ingest_move_frames: REJECTED - the tracker does ingest 0x09FD (29-49 MOVEENTRY frames per capture) and its projected cell always equals the frame's from-cell exactly (delta_from = [0,0] on every single frame).
answers_to_the_briefs_hypotheses.merge_across_mobs: REJECTED - the tracker keys the actor map by the wire AID (bl.id) and every probe frame's tracked cell matched its own mob; no cross-mob contamination was observed.
answers_to_the_briefs_hypotheses.freeze_at_spawn_or_spot: PARTLY TRUE, BUT NOT THE MECHANISM - the cell does freeze, but not at the spawn/spot cell: it freezes at the PRE-WALK cell of the mob's current walk, because the server emits one MOVEENTRY per walk and the tracker reads only that frame's from-cell.
answers_to_the_briefs_hypotheses.the_real_mechanism: the tracked mob cell lags the mob by up to 7 cells / ~6 s (the pre-walk cell), the tracked self cell leads the agent by up to 15 cells (the walk destination), the melee gate compares the two, and the server's 0x0139 rejection is invisible to production.

secondary_findings: ZC_NOTIFY_VANISH (0x0080) IS handled: native_gameplay._life (line 751-761) pops the actor, so a mob that walks out of the client's area disappears from the state's nearby list. The mob then re-enters with a fresh entry frame - which resets the tracked cell, so the agent re-approaches. The vanishes in the capture (2-7 per mob per 180 s) are the churn that makes the treadmill visible.

The client broadcast is area-bounded, not distance-bounded: rAthena's AREA_SIZE default is 14 cells (battle.cpp:8553), so a mob that crosses an area boundary is sent ZC_NOTIFY_VANISH (0x0080) and then re-enters with a fresh entry frame (0x09FD/0x09FF). In the capture the mobs walked 5-7 cells, crossed a boundary and vanished - which is also why the tracked cell sometimes refreshes unexpectedly.
The probe must send a keepalive: a clientless session that stops sending (CZ_REQUEST_TIME 0x0360 every 8 s) is dropped by the map server within ~60 s - the probe's first chase capture died that way.

conclusion: The mobs are not lost and their positions are not merged: the tracker reads every 0x09FD frame and its projected cell is byte-exact with that frame's from-cell. The staleness is structural: the pinned server emits ONE move frame per walk whose payload is (current cell, walk destination), the production tracker keeps the current cell for the mob and the walk destination for the agent, so the melee gate compares the agent's future cell with the mob's past cell. The server range-checks the real geometry with its circular client metric and answers 0x0139, which nothing in production ingests - so 138 swings can read 'adjacent' in the state, land nothing on the wire, and starve the economy exactly as observed.
